summary: The old harness has three preexisting coverage gaps: it always parses with entity processing enabled and the default whitespace mode, so it cannot exercise the supported alternatives. The destructor change and null guard change do not create a separate harness obligation.

claims.necessity_reason: The document constructor supports disabling entity processing, and text parsing uses that setting. The harness always constructs the default document, so no input can select the alternative mode.

before.requirement: Parse XML with processEntities=false so a recognized entity such as & is retained in the text value.
before.reason: The default constructor enables entity processing; the harness supplies no constructor argument.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: XMLText::ParseDeep reads the processEntities setting supplied by the cited XMLDocument constructor and selects the text parsing flags.
The selected destructor change concerns cleanup of nodes produced by this parsing mode.

after.requirement: Parse XML with processEntities=false so a recognized entity such as & is retained in the text value.
after.reason: The constructor and text parsing still support the mode, while the old harness still selects the default.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: XMLText::ParseDeep reads the processEntities setting supplied by the cited XMLDocument constructor and selects the text parsing flags.
The changed destructor cleans up nodes produced by this parsing mode.

claims.comparison_reason: Both versions expose the same constructor setting; the same default-only construction blocks it.

claims.necessity_reason: Text parsing supports COLLAPSE_WHITESPACE, but the harness fixes the document to the default preservation mode. XML containing repeated text whitespace is a finite trigger.

before.requirement: Parse text containing repeated whitespace with COLLAPSE_WHITESPACE selected.
before.reason: The harness cannot select the nondefault whitespace mode.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: XMLText::ParseDeep reads the whitespace mode supplied by the cited XMLDocument constructor and enables whitespace collapsing when COLLAPSE_WHITESPACE is selected.
The selected change alters cleanup of parsed nodes.

after.requirement: Parse text containing repeated whitespace with COLLAPSE_WHITESPACE selected.
after.reason: The mode remains supported, but the old harness still uses the default constructor.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: XMLText::ParseDeep reads the whitespace mode supplied by the cited XMLDocument constructor and enables whitespace collapsing when COLLAPSE_WHITESPACE is selected.
The selected change alters cleanup of parsed nodes.

claims.comparison_reason: The supported mode and the harness's fixed default are unchanged across the diff.

claims.necessity_reason: PEDANTIC_WHITESPACE preserves whitespace-only text immediately before a closing tag through a distinct DOM result. The harness cannot select that supported mode.

before.requirement: Parse an element such as <r>  </r> with PEDANTIC_WHITESPACE, retaining the whitespace text node.
before.reason: The harness constructs only a default PRESERVE_WHITESPACE document.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Declares the supported whitespace modes.
The constructor defaults to PRESERVE_WHITESPACE.
The selected change concerns cleanup of the resulting nodes.

after.requirement: Parse an element such as <r>  </r> with PEDANTIC_WHITESPACE, retaining the whitespace text node.
after.reason: The pedantic parsing path remains, while the old harness still uses the default mode.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Declares the supported whitespace modes.
The constructor defaults to PRESERVE_WHITESPACE.
The changed destructor cleans up the resulting nodes.

claims.comparison_reason: The parser's pedantic condition is unchanged and the same default-only harness blocks it on both sides.

claims.necessity_reason: Nested parsed nodes are already cleaned up through document destruction; the diff changes the cleanup path without establishing a missing target capability.

before.requirement: Destroy a parsed document containing nested nodes with valid ownership and cleanup.
before.reason: Parsing inserts nodes into the tree, and document destruction clears its children through the prior destructor path.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The document destructor invokes Clear.
Clear deletes the document's children and releases its parse buffer.

after.requirement: Destroy a parsed document containing nested nodes with valid ownership and cleanup.
after.reason: The changed destructor caches each next sibling, clears the child's parent, and deletes each child; document destruction still invokes Clear.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The document destructor invokes Clear.
Clear deletes the document's children and releases its parse buffer.

claims.comparison_reason: The local XMLDocument leaves scope after Parse on both sides, exercising cleanup without a harness change.

claims.necessity_reason: The changed null guard applies to a direct DeleteNode(nullptr) call. The harness invokes Parse, and its shown internal deletion path calls DeleteNode only after a node has been identified.

before.reason: The old harness makes no direct DeleteNode call; the parse path's deletion calls have a node.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: ParseDeep checks for an absent identified node before its error deletion call.

after.reason: Moving the null guard ahead of the assertion does not make a null call reachable from this harness.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: ParseDeep checks for an absent identified node before its error deletion call.

claims.comparison_reason: The direct null call is outside this entry point's operation on both sides.
